causalModel.founding: Bog iron forms in the ground here. Nails, tyres and tools wear out fast on the road. The road crews buy replacement iron from the diggers here.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The seep is stagnant and rich in iron. The diggers lift the ore from the mud in cakes.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The diggers come from three villages for one season a year. The diggers consider the work shameful.
causalModel.pressures: The seep is being worked out. Each season's cakes are smaller. Each season's cakes also lie further from the path.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The diggers would abandon the workings without ceremony.

districts.notes: One plank hut and a furnace floor on the level bench above the seep's north end.

why.what: The bench above the seep holds the diggers' hut and the furnace floor. The way down from the road crosses the bench.
why.whyHere: The diggers carry the seep's ore up to the first level ground. A furnace can stand dry on that ground.
why.whySpot: The bench is the last firm ground before the bank drops to the seep.
why.whyNeighbours: The keeper's lodge of the lower Onkobra is 95 m west. The porter yard at Red Cart is 200 m north-west.
why.playerPurpose: The bench is a place to take bog iron. The way down leads to the seep where LF67 starts.
why.microGeography: The bench is firm and level to within a degree. It falls east to a steep bank and the seep.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut's door turns east toward the furnace floor. The door also faces the way from the road.

why.what: The diggers' hut is a small plank house. Its posts are sunk in the bench. The crew's headman sleeps in the hut.
why.whyHere: The diggers come for one season. During that season the diggers need a roof near the furnace.
why.whySpot: The hut stands on the flattest part of the bench. It lies west of the furnace floor and clear of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The furnace floor is 15 m east of the hut. The way from the seep track ends at the hut's door.
why.playerPurpose: The hut is a shut room with beds. The crew keeps its stores in the hut.
why.microGeography: The plank house stands on a levelled pad on the bench. Its door is a step up from the ground.

playerPurpose.note: The season's crew know which end of the seep they stopped working. They also know what took the last digger who went there (LF67).
The stained boots in the hut are a clue to why the diggers stopped working the deep end of the seep.

parcels.orientationWhy: The furnace mouth faces west-south-west. Its charcoal bed also faces west-south-west. Both face the hut and the path in from the way.

playerPurpose.note: An ore digger works the furnace floor. The crew have stopped working the deep end of the seep. The reason for the stop is not stated.
Part of a quest takes place at the mound beside the furnace floor.

why.what: The furnace floor holds Skyrim's smelter, a crafting station. The smelter's kind is a pinned prop. Its 6.7 m plan is the furnace with its charcoal bed and slag bucket spread round it. The floor also holds bellows, fuel, ore and an ore cart.
why.whyHere: The diggers smelt ore where it is dug. Only iron is carried to the road.
why.whySpot: The furnace floor lies at the east end of the bench. It sits at the head of the bank above the seep.
why.whyNeighbours: The diggers' hut is just west of the furnace floor. The seep lies below the bank to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The furnace floor offers bog iron to take. The diggers break the furnace open each season to free the bloom.
why.microGeography: The furnace floor is levelled trodden earth on the bench. It falls away on the east to the bank over the seep.

routes.why: The route starts at the track on the seep's west shore. It climbs the bench past the furnace floor. It ends at the hut door.
The route runs from the way across the furnace floor. It ends at the furnace mouth.
The route runs from the way along the seep's south margin. It reaches the diggings, where the duckboards start.

approaches.sequence: The way leaves the track on the seep's west shore. It climbs north beside the water. The furnace shows first at the top of the rise. The hut shows beyond the furnace.
approaches.wayfinding: One way runs north from the track along the shore and up the bench. It passes the furnace floor. It ends at the hut door.

networkTerminals.why: The way leaves the track along the seep's west shore. It climbs north up the bench to the furnace floor and the hut.

combatSpaces.why: The levelled furnace floor is the one open footing between the hut and the bank.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The catalogue record is Bog Iron Workings. The record's class is works, magnitude M1. The occupants are D2 seasonal diggers, few. The interior is a dwelling S1 with one door.
scaleGrounding.why: A season's crew is three to six diggers from three villages. The workings are one sleeping hut with a furnace floor beside it.

candidates.why: The candidate is a level bench, firm and dry. It lies at the head of the bank above the seep's north end. It lies 25 m south of the road.
The candidate is the plotted anchor. It lies 60 m south on the seep's west shore.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The ground falls 6-8 degrees. It has no level cell for a hut pad. It lies 0.23 m over the water table.
